prompt: The query in the editor has one mistake. Fix it so that it counts the orders each store took in February 2025. order_ts holds UTC time: count orders from 1 February 2025 to 28 February 2025, UTC days, both included. Include every store, with 0 for a store that took none. Return two columns, in this order: store_code and n_orders. Return one row for each store. Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, move the month test so that it no longer removes stores.
In WHERE, the month test throws away the row that a store with no February order gets, because its order_ts is missing. In ON it only decides which orders match.
starter_sql:
SELECT s.store_code, COUNT(o.order_id) AS n_orders
FROM stores s
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.store_id = s.store_id
WHERE o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-02-01 00:00:00' AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-03-01 00:00:00'
GROUP BY s.store_code
why_this_works: A right-table test in WHERE turns a LEFT JOIN back into an inner join; in ON it filters the orders and keeps every store.
